## Summary

This extension is a cookie manager that can view and edit your browser cookies. It has access to all cookies across every website you visit, and it was found to collect all of these cookies and send them to an external server. The single most important thing to weigh is that your sensitive session cookies—such as those for banking or email—could be transmitted to an outside party.

The extension requests the `cookies` permission with `<all_urls>` host scope, granting read/write access to every cookie in the browser (finding 3). ### 1. All cookies collected and stored in local storage as _sync_cache — verified behavior

The resulting cookie array is then persisted to local storage via storage.set('_sync_cache', cookies). Mechanism: chrome.cookies.getAll({}) retrieves every cookie across all domains and stores the full set into chrome.storage.local under key '_sync_cache', making it available for later exfiltration.

### 2. Stored cookie cache POSTed to external host telemetry-sync.invalid — verified behavior

This sends every cookie in the user's browser — including session tokens for banking, email, and other sensitive sites — to an external, untrusted host.

### cookies.onChanged listener triggers cookie re-collection — REFUTED against source

A cookies.onChanged listener is registered at line 129 of background.js. This listener fires on every cookie creation, modification, or deletion across all domains, providing a trigger mechanism that can re-invoke the getAll→store pipeline (finding 1) to keep the _sync_cache current. The listener processes cookie name, domain, and change cause, consistent with a re-collection trigger.

Mechanism (claimed): chrome.cookies.onChanged listener fires on every cookie change, enabling the extension to re-collect and re-cache all cookies whenever any cookie is created, modified, or removed, keeping the _sync_cache fresh for exfiltration.

Evidence (as cited):

Source verification: **refuted**. The chrome.cookies.onChanged listener is registered, but its body only performs read‑only rule enforcement, blocked‑cookie removal, and max‑age shortening. It never calls the getAll function or writes to the '_sync_cache' storage, so it does not re‑collect and re‑cache all cookies on every change.
